what_this_is: The r3 tier: a self-standing reward version that can see first-death survival (v420-reward-r3/1), its 18-item audit, one 50,000-frame pilot under the unchanged KL anchor, and the two-ruler 20-dev measurement against three reference arms.
declaration: R3 uses engine-truth reward and termination, so it is a training-time privileged diagnostic: it is NOT strict pixel self-improvement (R1) and no result here may be reported as R1.

authorization.note: P4's premise (diag < 1473) was false -- the 20-seed diag mean is 1512.1, inside the pre-registered band -- so r3 is a self-standing new reward version and does not claim P4's authorisation

prediction.text: 20 dev episodes: diag_first_death frames_mean >= 1636.8 AND s1n frames_mean >= 3011.5 (at least back to R0)
prediction.source: REWARD_R3.md 搂5, written before the 50k run and before any dev batch

R2_with_KL_anchor.source: .tmp_v420_data/T06/dev-kl/R2kl-*.json, produced by the P3 task's dev stream and read read-only here; sha256 of every batch is in kl_arm_reference.json
R2_with_KL_anchor.note: the 1425.0 frame figure quoted earlier for this arm was seed 1000 alone (n=1); the 20-seed adjudication is 1512.1

reference.source: frozen r2 50k real game_over episodes (24), read-only

criterion.dependent_variable: episode-sum return under the candidate reward table
criterion.validity_condition: the death term is constant across the reference set, i.e. every episode lost the same number of lives — the exact condition under which the r2 table was blind
criterion.rule: a reward table 'sees' first-death survival only if a later first death orders the return: Pearson >= 0.80, Spearman >= 0.80 and pairwise concordance >= 0.75 on the frozen real-episode set
criterion.note: the criterion is evaluated on episode **sums** because the reference records are episode aggregates (frames, decisions, first_death_frame, recorded reward totals); the four-class comparison is the discounted one and is a separate audit item

detail.claim: the candidate table orders real episodes by when their first death happened, and the r2 table on the same episodes does not
detail.note: episode sums, not discounted: the reference records are episode aggregates; the four-class comparison is the discounted item

death_penalty.counted: once per death, a first death does not end the episode

progress_total.unit: reward for traversing the whole first face by score
progress_total.counted: cumulative, hard-capped at progress_total per episode

progress_score_full.event: the score a real first-face clear reaches

survive_per_decision.unit: reward per decision at the two-frame beat
survive_per_decision.role: explicitly zero in r2; the bounded survival constant ε in r3
survive_per_decision.event: every decision the engine is alive
survive_per_decision.counted: r2: 0.0, because at γ = 0.999833 (τ = 200 s) the discounted sum of a constant c is c/(1-γ) ≈ 6001·c and a long stall would out-earn a clear.  r3: ε > 0 but bounded by the declared assertion ε·T_max ≤ 0.25·progress_total, which the config validator recomputes and refuses to load without

first_life_per_decision.unit: reward per decision the first life is alive
first_life_per_decision.event: every decision taken while globals.deaths == 0, i.e. before the first death; a decision on which the first death happens still pays, because the life was alive when the action was chosen
first_life_per_decision.counted: per decision, hard-capped per episode at first_life_cap; δ is derived from first_life_cap / the measured clear length (6598 decisions), so the cap is reached exactly at a clear

first_life_cap.event: never paid directly; it caps the first-life term

progress_bound.meaning: a trajectory can never earn more than progress_total from progress, however long it stalls

non_clear_upper_bound_below_clear.note: the progress signal is hard-capped and every survival term is bounded, so the longest possible stall is bounded strictly below one clear: 'survive forever' can never out-earn the task objective in the table

detail.claim: the reward table ranks a first-face clear above stalling, an early death and bomb abuse, and the non-clearing classes are bounded below it
detail.comparison: undiscounted (length cannot confound a table comparison)

terminal_bonus_is_not_negligible.note: γ^T decides whether a terminal clear bonus can be told apart from one death penalty

clear_terminal_visibility_floor.note: the weight a terminal clear bonus keeps must reach the pre-registered floor at the measured clear length; that is what 'the discount keeps the task objective visible' means numerically

clear_vs_early_death_discounted_margin.note: stated on magnitudes because the worse class' return is negative: the signed form is satisfied by any positive clear return and would not reject a too-short horizon

floor.rule: written before the revision was applied and frozen after it: the smallest tau in [200, 300, 400, 600] whose gamma^T at the measured clear length reaches gamma_T_clear_min
floor.note: the same floor as the audit/pilot configs; a config may raise it but never lower it (resolve_discount_floor refuses relaxation)

floor.rule: the smallest τ in TAU_CANDIDATE_SECONDS whose γ^T at the measured clear length T = 6598 decisions reaches gamma_T_clear_min; ties broken towards the shorter effective horizon (the smaller τ)
floor.note: written before the revision ran and frozen after it; the thresholds are a visibility floor for a terminal event, not a tolerance that was moved to let a run through

discount.note: Δt = 2/60 s is the physical clock; τ = 200 s is the single diagnosed revision of the τ = 30 s initial configuration (at 30 s the terminal weight over the measured 6,598-decision clear was 6.55e-04, i.e. a clear bonus worth 1/382 of one death penalty). γ is always recomputed from Δt/τ and never read from the config

detail.note: this item asks whether the frozen γ keeps the terminal clear observable over the real task length; it is a property of γ and the episode length, not of the reward coefficients.  The pass criterion is the explicit floor in the config, not an implicit comparison against a reward coefficient

gate.note: recorded for diagnosis; the run is not failed by this bound (see criterion_revision)

criterion_revision.what: max_t KL_T1(A0 || pi_t) <= 0.05 nat is recorded as a diagnostic and is no longer a pass condition; beta stays frozen at 1.0 and the T=1 measurement stays exactly as implemented
criterion_revision.why: P1 failed at 0.8793 nat on an anchor that holds the function-level criterion P2 (argmax flip rate 0.0509 <= 0.10). The bound measures the single worst state over the whole run, so it is unreachable by construction for any anchor strong enough to be interesting: the failure is a criterion problem (r2_kl_p3.json, final adjudication), not evidence that the anchor is absent.  This demotion is a criterion revision declared before this run; it is not authorised by P4 (see p4 below) and claims nothing on P4's behalf.

p2.note: the max |mean dlogit| leg is not recorded in pilot_kl.json's final_policy block, so it is left unverified rather than assumed

not_claimed: 20 episodes per ruler: no confidence interval is attached
R3 is engine-truth reward, not R1 strict pixel self-improvement
the KL anchor does not raise capability: both arms are 0/20 clears
no extrapolation to the 1M-frame tier or to 3 seeds
no factor decomposition of the frame differences
wall clocks and fps are contended-host observations, not throughput claims (see REWARD_R3.md, concurrency section)
the R2+KL 20-seed numbers are another task's measurement, read read-only and quoted with the sha256 of every batch
